findings.title: Denial cache keys omit the identity type
findings.description:
The key uses `checkReq.UserUID` but omits `checkReq.IdentityType`. Subjects such as `anonymous:0` and `render:0` therefore share denial entries for the same action, name, and folder.

For example, an anonymous denial for a dashboard would also deny a subsequent renderer request for that dashboard, bypassing `getRendererPermissions`, which grants dashboard reads. Include the identity type or complete subject in the key, and add a regression test covering these two subjects.

findings.title: Undelimited tuple encoding permits denial-key collisions
findings.description:
Joining resource names and parent UIDs with underscores does not uniquely encode the request. For the same namespace, user, and action, `(name="a_b", parent="c")` and `(name="a", parent="b_c")` produce identical keys. These fields are passed through without validation that excludes underscores.

A denial for one resource can consequently deny access to another until expiration. Use an unambiguous encoding, such as a serialized tuple or length-prefixed components, and test colliding inputs.

findings.title: Denial-precedence test does not seed an allowing permission
findings.description:
The test claims to seed an allowing permission to prove the denial cache takes precedence, but sets `"dashboards:uid:dash1"` to `false`. `checkPermission` only treats a `true` value as a grant, so this does not establish the intended competing allow condition.

Set the permission to `true` so the test verifies that an explicit cached denial overrides an otherwise successful permission check.
